title: Acknowledging an Opposing Viewpoint
summary: إزاي تذكر رأي الناحية التانية بأدب وتعترف بيه، وبعدين ترد عليه وترجع لرأيك، باستخدام Although / Despite / However.

blocks.text: الدرس ده عن إيه؟

text: A strong speaker does not pretend the other side does not exist. You **acknowledge** (admit) the opposing view politely, then **respond** to it and show why your opinion is still stronger. This is called **conceding** and **refuting**.

blocks.text: الدرس ده عن مهارة بتخلي كلامك **مقنع ومحترم** في نفس الوقت: إنك تذكر **رأي الناحية التانية** وتعترف إن فيه جزء صح، وبعدين ترد عليه وترجع لرأيك. زي ما تقول لصاحبك: «ماشي، عندك حق إن الأونلاين أسرع، **بس** المحل أضمن».

الكتاب بيطلب المهارة دي في وحدات كتير: **Unit 2** (*acknowledge counter-arguments*)، **Unit 3** (*recognize an opposing viewpoint* + **concession clauses**)، و**Units 6 – 10** كل presentation فيها جملة *Although some people believe…, I think…* وفيها سؤال **Concede / Acknowledge**. وفي **Unit 4** (Black Friday) الكتاب بيقول: اعترف بفايدة واحدة وبعدين **على طول** وضّح إن الضرر أكبر.
ليه أذكر رأي اللي ضدي؟

text: When you mention the other side, you show that you are **fair**, **informed** and **confident**. Your listener trusts you more. But do not stop there: you must always **answer** the opposing view.

items: بيبين إنك **فاهم الموضوع كويس** وعارف كل جوانبه، مش بتتكلم من ناحية واحدة.
بيخليك **عادل (fair)** ومش متحيز (biased)، والكتاب في Unit 1 و2 بيكلمك كتير عن الـ bias.
بيقفل الطريق على اللي قدامك: إنت قلت حجته قبله ورديت عليها.
**بس خلي بالك:** لو ذكرت الرأي التاني وما ردتش عليه، كأنك بتقول إن هو اللي صح!

blocks.text: الخطوات التلاتة: اعترف ← رد ← ارجع لرأيك

rows: اذكر رأي الناحية التانية وقول إن فيه حاجة صح
Some people believe that… / It is true that… / Admittedly,…
وضّح ليه الرأي ده مش كافي أو فيه مشكلة، ويُفضل بدليل
However,… / Nevertheless,… / But the problem is that…
That is why I still believe… / So, overall,…

items.en: Some people believe that online shopping saves time.
items.ar: ١. اعترف: في ناس شايفة إن الشراء أونلاين بيوفر وقت.

items.en: However, free returns mean that many items are sent back and destroyed.
items.ar: ٢. رد: بس الإرجاع المجاني معناه إن حاجات كتير بترجع وتتدمر.

items.en: That is why I still believe returns should be limited.
items.ar: ٣. ارجع لرأيك: علشان كده أنا لسه شايف إن الإرجاع لازم يكون محدود.

blocks.title: حيلة للحفظ: «آه… بس… علشان كده»
blocks.text: في الكلام بالعربي بنعمل كده كل يوم: «**آه** صح… **بس**… **علشان كده**…». في الإنجليزي: **It is true that… / However,… / That is why…**. لو حفظت التلاتة دول هتعرف ترد على أي رأي.
القواعد: جمل الاعتراف (Concession Clauses)

text: Concession words introduce the idea you are admitting. **Although / Even though / While** are followed by a full clause (subject + verb). **Despite / In spite of** are followed by a noun or -ing.

blocks.text: دي نفس الكلمات اللي في جدول الكتاب في **Unit 3** (Concession Clauses)، بس هنا هنشرح إزاي كل واحدة بييجي بعدها إيه بالظبط، لأن ده أكتر حتة الطلاب بيغلطوا فيها:

rows: **Although** the GEM is very large, visitors find their way easily.
**While it is true that** gaming is fun, it can reduce sleep.
**Despite** its modern design, the museum focuses on ancient history.
**Admittedly**, solar panels are expensive at first. However, they save money later.
**It may be argued that** digital tours are convenient. Nevertheless, visiting in person is unique.
**Some people claim that** hobbies waste time. However, they reduce stress.

blocks.title: أشهر الأخطاء (غلط ← صح)
items: ✗ **Although** fast fashion is cheap, **but** it harms the planet. ← ✓ **Although** fast fashion is cheap, it harms the planet. (مينفعش although و but مع بعض)
✗ **Despite** it is expensive, … ← ✓ **Despite** the high price, … / ✓ **Although** it is expensive, … (despite بعدها اسم مش جملة)
✗ **Despite of** the rain, … ← ✓ **Despite** the rain, … / ✓ **In spite of** the rain, … (of مع in spite بس)
✗ تذكر الرأي التاني وتسكت ← ✓ لازم ترد عليه بـ However وتقول ليه رأيك أقوى.
✗ *You are wrong!* (قلة ذوق) ← ✓ *I understand your point, but…* (رد مؤدب)
✗ تعترف بحاجة تهد رأيك كله ← ✓ اعترف بنقطة **صغيرة** وبعدين وضّح إن نقطتك أكبر.

blocks.text: لما بترد على شخص قدامك (في المناقشة أو الديبيت)

text: In a conversation, be polite. First show that you heard the other person, then give your view. Never attack the person, only discuss the idea.

blocks.text: في الـ presentation إنت بتذكر «بعض الناس». لكن في الـ discussion أو الـ debate أو الـ role-play فيه **شخص قدامك** قال رأي. هنا لازم تبقى مؤدب: ابدأ بإنك سمعته وفاهمه، وبعدين قول رأيك. الكتاب في **Unit 6** (The Wetland Meeting) و**Unit 10** (The Convincing Post) بيدي جمل زي دي:

groups.title: الاعتراف في الـ presentation
items: Although some people believe that …, I think …
Some people argue that … However, …
It is true that … but …
Admittedly, … However, …
While it is true that …, …
It may be argued that … Nevertheless, …

groups.title: الرد على شخص قدامك (مؤدب)
items: I understand your concern, but …
I see what you mean. However, …
That's a fair point, but …
I understand why you're doubtful, but …
You're right that …, but have you considered …?
I agree with you up to a point, but …

groups.title: رد قوي بدليل (Refuting)
items: However, the evidence shows that …
The problem with this view is that …
This ignores the fact that …
Nevertheless, …
Even so, …

groups.title: الرجوع لرأيك
items: That is why I still believe …
So, overall, the benefits are greater.
Even so, my view remains that …
While other views exist, … remains more convincing.

groups.title: الوصول لحل وسط (Compromise)
items: A fair compromise might be …
A balanced approach may be the best solution.
Perhaps both sides could agree that …

blocks.text: ثلاث طرق للرد على الرأي التاني
بعد ما تعترف، فيه ٣ طرق ترد بيها. اختار المناسبة:

rows: Black Friday saves some money, **but** the waste and debt it causes are much bigger.
Some say one person cannot help. **However**, Farida's Nile clean-up grew from five friends to over two hundred volunteers.
Hobbies can take time, **but** only ten minutes a day is enough to make progress.

blocks.text: إجابة نموذجية (Model Answer)
ده جزء من presentation زي اللي في **Unit 3** و**Unit 7** (*Although some people believe…, I think…*). الموضوع: هل المدارس المفروض تمنع الموبايل؟ لاحظ الخطوات التلاتة:

blocks.title: Model spoken answer: opinion + opposing view (about 1 minute)
blocks.task: Should schools ban mobile phones during the school day? Give your opinion and recognise an opposing viewpoint.
text: In my opinion, schools should ban mobile phones during lessons. This is because notifications break students' concentration, and it takes time to focus again after every message.

**Admittedly**, phones can be useful. Some people believe that students need them to search for information or to call their parents in an emergency. I understand this concern, and it is a fair point.

**However**, schools already have computers for research, and parents can call the school office if something urgent happens. **Even though** phones are helpful, they distract students far more often than they help them in class.

**That is why I still believe** a ban during lessons is the right choice. A fair compromise might be to let students use their phones during breaks, so they stay connected without losing focus in class.
notes: **البداية:** رأي واضح (*In my opinion*) وسبب (*This is because*).
**الاعتراف:** *Admittedly* و*Some people believe that* وذكر سببين حقيقيين للناحية التانية (البحث والطوارئ). وقال *it is a fair point* علشان يبان عادل.
**الرد:** *However* ورد على **كل** سبب من الاتنين (كمبيوتر المدرسة / تليفون المكتب). وكمان استخدم *Even though + clause* صح من غير but.
**الرجوع للرأي:** *That is why I still believe* وبعدها **حل وسط** (*A fair compromise might be…*) زي ما الكتاب بيطلب في الديبيت.
الكلام مرتب في ٤ أجزاء، وكل جزء جملتين أو تلاتة بس: سهل تقوله من غير ما تقرأ.

blocks.text: إزاي بييجي في الأسئلة؟
الأسئلة في الكتاب والمراجعات بتيجي بالأشكال دي:
**١) جزء Concede / Acknowledge في الـ Presentation** (Units 6 – 10):

text: What does your example concede or acknowledge about the genuine needs of local communities?

blocks.text: **الحل:** اعترف بحاجة حقيقية للناحية التانية: *Although wetlands must be protected, I acknowledge that fishermen depend on them for their daily income. A fair solution would be to allow fishing in some seasons only.*
**٢) Concede ثم conclusion** (Unit 7 و10 — fact-checker):

text: Concede: Although some brands are making genuine improvements, many use vague language. Then give your conclusion.

blocks.text: **الحل:** ابدأ بنفس جملة Although، وبعدين قول نتيجتك: *So before believing a "100% sustainable" post, we should look for real details about materials and factories.*
**٣) سؤال جرامر على الـ concession** (MCQ أو اكتب الجملة تاني) — زي التمرين A تحت.
تدريب
**A) Choose the correct answer from a, b, c or d.**

items.q:
1. ______ screen time can be educational, too much of it harms sleep.
a. Despite
b. Although
c. However
d. In spite of
items.a: **b** — بعدها جملة كاملة (screen time can be…)، يبقى Although. Despite وIn spite of بعدهم اسم.

items.q:
2. ______ the high cost, many families are installing solar heaters.
a. Although
b. Even though
c. Despite
d. While it is true
items.a: **c** — بعدها اسم (the high cost)، يبقى Despite.

items.q:
3. Although the museum is crowded, ______ it is worth visiting.
a. but
b. however
c. (nothing)
d. so
items.a: **c** — مفيش but أو however بعد Although في نفس الجملة.

items.q:
4. "Some people claim that hobbies waste time. ______, they help us relax."
a. However
b. Although
c. Because
d. For example
items.a: **a** — جملة جديدة فيها رد على الرأي التاني، يبقى However.

items.q:
5. Which is the most polite reply in a discussion?
a. That's a silly idea.
b. You are completely wrong.
c. I see what you mean, but the evidence shows something different.
d. No.
items.a: **c** — بتعترف إنك فاهم، وبعدين ترد بدليل.

items.q:
6. In spite ______ the rain, the volunteers cleaned the beach.
a. to
b. of
c. that
d. (nothing)
items.a: **b** — in spite **of**. (لكن despite من غير of)

blocks.text: **B) Rewrite the sentences using the word(s) in brackets.**

items.q: 7. Fast fashion is cheap. It causes pollution. (Although)
items.a: **Although** fast fashion is cheap, it causes pollution.

items.q: 8. The weather was hot. The students joined the clean-up. (Despite)
items.a: **Despite** the hot weather, the students joined the clean-up.

items.q: 9. Vocational education is sometimes undervalued. It prepares students for real jobs. (While it is true that)
items.a: **While it is true that** vocational education is sometimes undervalued, it prepares students for real jobs.

items.q: 10. Digital tours are convenient. Visiting in person is a unique experience. (It may be argued that … Nevertheless)
items.a: **It may be argued that** digital tours are convenient. **Nevertheless**, visiting in person is a unique experience.

items.q: 11. Correct the mistake: "Although the app is free, but it collects users' data."
items.a: Although the app is free, it collects users' data. — اشيل but.

items.q: 12. Correct the mistake: "Despite it was late, she finished her project."
items.a: **Although** it was late, she finished… **أو** **Despite** the late hour, she finished… — despite مينفعش بعدها جملة.

blocks.text: **C) Your partner says the sentence below. Acknowledge it politely, then respond.**

items.q: 13. "Brands are good because they guarantee quality."
items.a: *That's a fair point, but* many cheaper products have the same quality. We often pay extra only for the logo.

items.q: 14. "One person can't stop climate change."
items.a: *I understand your concern, but* small actions add up. For example, a Nile clean-up started with five friends and grew to hundreds of volunteers.

items.q: 15. "Students are too busy for hobbies."
items.a: *I see what you mean. However,* ten or fifteen minutes a day is enough, and a hobby can actually reduce exam stress.

items.q: 16. "Free returns are fair to customers."
items.a: *You're right that* they make shopping easier, *but* many returned items are destroyed. *A fair compromise might be* free returns only for faulty products.

items.q: 17. "Farmers should protect their crops by any method."
items.a: *I agree with you up to a point, but* some methods harm wildlife. *A fair rule would be that* both sides use safe fences and wildlife corridors.

blocks.text: **D) Speaking practice: قول رأيك + اعترف بالرأي التاني + رد عليه.** (أفكار نموذجية)

items.q: 18. (Unit 2) Should schools restrict students' use of social media?
items.a: **Opinion:** yes, during school hours. **Concede:** Admittedly, it helps students share homework. **Respond:** However, school platforms can do that without endless scrolling. **Back:** So a limit is still better.

items.q: 19. (Unit 3) Should old buildings be replaced by modern ones?
items.a: **Opinion:** no, they should be preserved. **Concede:** It is true that modern buildings are safer. **Respond:** However, old buildings keep our collective memory. **Back:** Restoring them is a balanced approach.

items.q: 20. (Unit 4) Do brands influence teenagers more than parents?
items.a: **Opinion:** yes, in shopping choices. **Concede:** Although parents shape values, … **Respond:** brands reach teenagers online all day. **Back:** That is why brand influence is stronger in what they buy.

items.q: 21. (Unit 5) Is renewable energy too expensive for Egypt?
items.a: **Opinion:** no. **Concede:** Admittedly, solar parks cost a lot to build. **Respond:** However, the price of solar panels has fallen a lot, and the sun is free. **Back:** So it saves money in the long term.

items.q: 22. (Unit 6) Should a wetland be used for new housing?
items.a: **Opinion:** no, it should be protected. **Concede:** I understand that people need homes. **Respond:** But migratory birds and fishermen depend on it. **Back:** Housing can be built on land that is less important.

items.q: 23. (Unit 7) Does turning a hobby into a job kill the enjoyment?
items.a: **Opinion:** not always. **Concede:** Although pressure can reduce enjoyment, … **Respond:** setting limits keeps it fun. **Back:** So passion can stay alive if it is balanced.

items.q: 24. (Unit 9) Do online friendships give a real sense of belonging?
items.a: **Opinion:** partly. **Concede:** It is true that online groups support people who feel alone. **Respond:** However, face-to-face friends notice when we are sad. **Back:** So both are useful, but real-life belonging is deeper.

items.q: 25. (Unit 10) Is buying second-hand clothes a good idea?
items.a: **Opinion:** yes. **Concede:** Some people believe second-hand clothes are low quality. **Respond:** However, many are almost new, and swap events check quality. **Back:** That is why I still think it is smart and sustainable.

blocks.title: ملخص الدرس في سطرين
items: ٣ خطوات: **اعترف** (*Some people believe / Admittedly*) ← **رد** (*However / Nevertheless*) ← **ارجع لرأيك** (*That is why I still believe*).
**Although / Even though / While** + جملة كاملة، و**Despite / In spite of** + اسم أو -ing.
مينفعش **Although … but** في نفس الجملة، ومينفعش **Despite of**.
مع شخص قدامك: ابدأ بـ *I understand your concern, but…* وناقش الفكرة مش الشخص.
لو ممكن، اقفل بـ **حل وسط**: *A fair compromise might be…*
